writeup: TIC 246860059 is a candidate eclipsing binary star identified through automated analysis of TESS photometry. The system shows a primary eclipse with a depth of 2.00 percent occurring every 7.0111 days, detected with a signal-to-noise ratio of 29.8 using the Box Least Squares algorithm. Pixel-level image analysis provides additional support, revealing a difference-imaging peak signal-to-noise of 5.5, though the centroid offset of 16.2 arcseconds from the target warrants further investigation. No secondary eclipse was detected in the data. The object does not appear in six major variable-star catalogs, suggesting it may be previously unknown to the scientific literature. The automated machine-learning screening assigned this candidate a score of 0.39, reflecting moderate confidence that this represents a genuine astrophysical source rather than an instrumental artifact.
